units.translation: 21 δ᾽ raises the question... whether the number of Athenaeus (δ᾽ for δύο) or that of the scholiast (δ〈ευτέρα〉 for δ᾽) should be corrected
24 Et. Gen. (A²B) ἐλεπσίδας: I 1266. πίσσεα are the wet places. ἐλεπσίδας: some [say] the [places] with trees,
24 οἱ μὲν — ἀνέμου in Gm

others the marshy and muddy places, but better the 〈rough and〉 rocky places, from being worn away by sun and wind and rain. Whence also λέπα [means] the peaks of mountains: Euripides (Phoen. 24) 'and the crags of Cithaeron'.

2 1279. Et. Gen. (AB) Ποσειδεῖον: . . . but the Poseideion is a cape of Mysia, as in I 1279. 3 Et. Gen. (B) χαροπός: very joyful, bright-eyed. From which χαροπὴ in Apollonius: I 1280—81. διαλάμπουσιν· from which γλαυκῶπις [epithet of] Athena. περάτη now [means] the east; but it can also be said of the west and of the north and south as περάτη: for each of these, lying opposite the angle of the other part of the sky, is a boundary and end. Et. Gen. (AB) γλαύσσουσι: I 1281. Instead of λάμπουσιν· from which also γλαυκῶπις. περάτη now [means] the east; but it can also be said of the west and of the north and south as περάτη and end. 6 Epim. Hom. (Cram. An. Ox.
